stature.source: Useful Tropical Plants: recorded to 69 m (its table 58 m), bole diameter to 230 cm; Wikipedia: an immense emergent to 80 m; read 2026-11-05

targets.from: judgement values from the drafter's reading of the sources and knowledge of the species (2026-11-05), no photographs measured; to be replaced by photo measurements: an immense straight bole over steep buttresses, a large globose emergent crown of glossy lance-shaped leaves, its sub-crowns separated by narrow gaps (crown shyness)

young.note: a pole in the understorey or a gap: a straight slender stem with a narrow, monopodial crown of tiers of horizontal branches (Roux's model), waiting for light

veteran.note: an emergent giant: a huge pale bole with towering plank buttresses, the crown a few massive limbs bearing cauliflower clumps of leaves high above the canopy

description: An immense emergent of Danum's hillsides and ridges, 45-65 m tall and more, with a massive straight bole up to two metres thick above large buttresses and a big, globose crown of glossy, lance-shaped leaves with fine parallel veins. The wood smells of camphor; the crowns of neighbouring kapur keep a narrow gap of sky between them.

season_notes.winter: Evergreen; new leaf flushes red-bronze on some crowns.
season_notes.spring: Evergreen; in a mast year a crown of small white flowers.
season_notes.summer: Evergreen; in a mast year the five-winged fruits spinning down (seed collected in September).

range.where: endemic to Borneo; undisturbed mixed dipterocarp forest on hillsides and ridges, sandy soils to 400 m or clay-rich soils on volcanics and shale to 700 m (UTP); at Danum common on the slopes and ridges

notes: COMPROMISES: there is no dipterocarp, no tropical tree and no tree over 45 m with a broadleaf crown in the library; black cottonwood is the template for its tall straight bole only. The trunk patch makes the bole run clear to about 0.55 of the height, then fork into three limbs under a flat, wide, 'cauliflower' crown envelope, and the buttresses are the root-flare primitive (trunk.flare 2.4, roots.buttress 0.95, 3-6 buttresses, 2.2 times the default flare height): real plank buttresses run 2-4 m up the bole and several metres out, thin and steep-sided, which the flare's rounded fins approximate only in the near tier (the mid tier draws one ring, the far impostors none). The crown's clumped, 'broccoli' sub-crowns of reiterated limbs are the template's clumps, not a modelled reiteration. Under a 60 m tree the scale of everything (bark tiles, leaf cards, LOD budgets) is the cottonwood's at 1.6 times, untested in the lineup. Heights and diameter from Useful Tropical Plants and Wikipedia; the large globose crown and the hillside and ridge habitat from UTP. Buttress form, bark (drawn 'furrowed' grey-brown; the real bark flakes in irregular pieces and needs a local look) and the lance-shaped leaves with close parallel secondary veins are the drafter's knowledge. Crown shyness (the narrow gaps between neighbouring crowns, famous in Dryobalanops) cannot be expressed: the species mix places trees independently and the generator does not know its neighbours. Seed collected in September (a UTP commenter). Danum is aseasonal: evergreen, no leaf-off, colours constant through the four calendar seasons except for small flushes of new red-bronze leaves. Dipterocarps flower and fruit together in irregular mast years every two to ten years, after an El Nino dry spell; the game's seasons cannot express a mast year, so no flowers or fruit are drawn and the seed entries in eaten_by are marked as mast-year food. Animals as for white seraya (drafter's knowledge, not in the library). Region tag borneo is not yet a natural region in pipeline/regions.py.
